items.how: Long Section C question on ammonia: (a)(i) calculate Kp (with units) at 450 K and 2 atm when 20% of 1 mol N2 with 3 mol H2 is converted (6); (a)(ii) give the equation linking Kp and Delta S total and calculate Delta S total (2); (b) titration of 25.0 cm3 of 1.00 mol dm-3 ammonia with 0.625 mol dm-3 HCl: volume at equivalence (2), ionic equation (1) and Ka expression (1) for NH4+, pH of 0.385 mol dm-3 NH4Cl (3), draw the titration curve (4), and judge thymol blue as indicator (2).
items.ms: (a)(i) equilibrium moles N2 0.80, H2 2.4, NH3 0.40; partial pressures 0.444, 1.333, 0.222 atm; Kp = p(NH3)^2/(p(N2) x p(H2)^3) = 0.0469 atm-2 (marks for moles, mole fractions, partial pressures, expression and value, units). (iii) Ka = [NH3][H3O+]/[NH4+]. (iv) [H+] = sqrt(5.6 x 10-10 x 0.385) = 1.47 x 10-5, pH 4.83. (v) curve from pH 11.6 to below pH 3 with a vertical section at 40 cm3 starting between pH 9 and 7 and 3-5 units long. items.ms: (a)(i) fewer gas moles on the right so high pressure favours methanol (or more collisions raise the rate); (ii) exothermic so low temperature favours yield, a compromise temperature gives a fast enough rate; (iii) catalyst allows lower temperature or is selective/reusable. (iv) high Ea / slow when cold, warm to speed up, Mn2+ autocatalyses. (v) 4.04e-4 mol MnO4-, x5/2 x10 = 0.0101 mol acid, water mass 0.361 g, ratio 1:2 so x = 2.

items.name: Method to confirm first Ka of ethanedioic acid
items.how: Outline a practical method, using the indicator data and a pH meter with equimolar acid and NaOH, to confirm Ka1 = 5.6 x 10-2 mol dm-3 (pKa1 = 1.25); no calculations required.
items.ms: Any three points from two methods. Method 1: titrate the acid with NaOH to the first end-point using thymol blue (1), then add half the titre volume of NaOH to a fresh sample and measure its pH with a pH meter (1). Method 2: add NaOH in portions noting pH each time (1) past the first sharp pH rise (1), plot pH against volume and read the pH at half-neutralisation (= pKa1) (1); phenolphthalein is not acceptable.
